owner_policy.quote: nothing should be paid … cut the probes and make them free.
owner_policy.scope: This repo's own automation: anything a workflow, a script or an agent in this repository runs. The Time2Read product's own inference is a separate named lane below, funded by subscriptions, and is not governed by max_cost_usd.

policy.on_reported_cost: throw PaidCostError and fail the run

pricing_snapshot.selection: strongest general instruct models among the $0 list, largest context first. Excluded: google/lyria-3-* (music, and not :free so it can turn paid silently), nvidia/nemotron-3.5-content-safety:free (safety classifier), poolside/laguna-* and cohere/north-mini-code:free (code-only), liquid/lfm-2.5-2.6b:free (sub-10B), openrouter/free (non-deterministic meta-router), and thinkingmachines/inkling*:free (403 "only available on agentic harnesses" on a sibling repo's first live dispatch, 11 Oct 2026).

automation_lane.detail: No script or workflow in this repository calls a model. The Search Console collectors, the prerender check and the IndexNow submitter are all deterministic. The router exists so that the first one to need a model has a $0 door to go through instead of naming its own.

paid_lanes.purpose: The Time2Read product itself: adaptive story generation, narration, speech-to-text, spelling correction, translation, dictionary lookups and illustration.
paid_lanes.why_not_free: Subscribers pay for this inference; it is cost of goods, not an unattended probe. The owner's zero-paid rule is about automation this repo runs on a schedule, and this lane runs only when a paying reader opens a story.
paid_lanes.guard: src/test/guards/zero-paid-llm.test.ts keeps this lane listed here, so a new paid call site cannot appear unrecorded.
paid_lanes.free_dictionary: api.dictionaryapi.dev, no key, $0: word-dictionary's last tier before a built-in entry (supabase/functions/_shared/wordFallback.ts)

text_chain.quote: i'd rather use the openrouter free ... i dont wanna pay anything if possible
text_chain.applies_to: story pages (generate-adaptive-story), end-of-story quizzes (generate-quiz), word-dictionary, translate-universal, correct-spelling
text_chain.privacy_rule: Before any request leaves on tiers 1-3, every child's name (and names found in the prompt's Character Info: name, parent, sibling, school, city) is replaced with a placeholder (Kiki, Lulu, ...) and put back in the returned text: supabase/functions/_shared/deidentify.ts. No email or ids are ever in a prompt. OpenAI (tier 4, paid, no training on API data) receives the request as written.

order.rotation: next model on 429, 5xx, a 20 s timeout or an empty answer; a 401 ends the tier
order.tested_2026_10_26: nemotron-3-ultra: 200, good 2nd-grade prose and valid JSON (~4-5 s). gemma-4-31b and gemma-4-26b: 429 upstream rate limit at test time (kept: free capacity varies by hour). nemotron-3-super: 404 at test time (kept last). Rejected: thinkingmachines/inkling:free (403, agentic harnesses only), nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning:free (200 with empty text: reasoning eats the budget).
order.terms_check: OpenRouter terms (openrouter.ai/terms, read 26 Oct 2026): the account holder must be 18+ (the owner is); no clause forbids a service used by children. Model licences: Gemma Terms of Use and NVIDIA Open Model License carry no age restriction on the downstream service. Free endpoints may log prompts, hence the privacy rule.

Cloudflare terms (cloudflare.com/website-terms, read 26 Oct 2026): no under-18 prohibition, only a note that the services are not COPPA/CIPA compliance tools. Meta Llama 3.3 Acceptable Use Policy has no age restriction on the service. The vault's CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN answered 401 on Workers AI, so this tier needs a token with the Workers AI permission.

order.spend_rule: prepaid credit only (owner added $10, auto top-up off); a 402 skips this tier for 10 minutes; provider.data_collection = deny
order.terms_check: OpenRouter terms as above; Meta Llama 3.3 licence and AUP: no age restriction on the downstream service.

models: as the caller names them (gpt-5 chain for stories, gpt-4o-mini for words)
order.spend_rule: last paid resort; a no-credit or bad-key refusal skips it for 10 minutes
order.terms_check: OpenAI services agreement allows business API use for a children's product with the operator responsible for COPPA consent (time-2-read collects parental consent); API data is not used for training.

order.what: Backup Mode pre-written stories; word-dictionary: free dictionary (api.dictionaryapi.dev) then a kind built-in entry

excluded.why: Gemini API Additional Terms (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms): not for services directed towards or likely to be accessed by individuals under 18.

Serves Google Gemini models (google/gemini-*), so the same Gemini restriction applies. Removed from the text chain 26 Oct 2026; generate-quiz and the image-prompt helper still call it (separate follow-up).

Not added: no key on the project. Groq terms page gave no readable age clause (needs a manual read); Cerebras terms require the account holder to be 13+ with no child-service clause found. Each needs an owner signup (console.groq.com/keys, cloud.cerebras.ai) before it can be a tier.
